newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CARLING DISCOUNTS REPORTS OF RETIREMENT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CARLING DISCOUNTS REPORTS OF RETIREMENT.

text.p: Former England captain Will Carling on Sunday discounted reports that he was retiring from international rugby.
Carling, who featured in England's Triple Crown success against Wales on Saturday, wrote in the Mail on Sunday that he was still eager to play, perhaps through to the 1999 World Cup.
"I'm a long way from retiring from international rugby -- don't rule me out of another trip to Cardiff Arms Park when it is rebuilt," he wrote in his regular column for the paper.
"If I decide to carry on it will only be because I can play for two more seasons and take part in another World Cup."
Carling, who captained England 59 times in his 72 tests, has already ruled himself out of contention for the British Lions tour to South Africa and England's tour to Argentina.
But he stressed that a few months break from the game could see him return refreshed and ready for international rugby in the new season.
"I really have not made up my mind. Assuming that the selectors still want me then England may not have seen the last of me," he said.
